content: FlClash desktop: Go core runs as a separate process (CGO_ENABLED=0); Flutter UI talks to it over local IPC — Unix domain socket on Linux/macOS, named pipe on Windows (transport primitives in plugins/rust_api Rust plugin; Dart owns correlation/lifecycle in lib/core/desktop/). Framing: 4-byte little-endian length prefix, max 64 MiB, JSON envelope CoreMethodCall(id,method,args)/CoreMethodResponse(id,result,error). Reverse-direction events (traffic/logs/state) pushed from core via three queues in core/message.go: state queue never drops, priority/bulk queues evict only their own oldest; a batcher flushes every 16 ms or 32 messages; events never block the core. Android instead embeds the core in-process (libclash.so via JNI). Verified across repo docs/architecture.md, DeepWiki, and project wiki — three independent sources.
